equations.name: equidistant fisheye ray angle
equations.purpose: Maps the circular 180 degree fisheye from zenith at center to horizon at the edge.

equations.name: Figure 1 four skydome scene set
equations.expression: rows = {06h00 / theta_s=87 deg, 10h15 / theta_s=41 deg, 11h15 / theta_s=31 deg, 13h15 / theta_s=21 deg}; sun_altitude = 90 deg - theta_s; sun_azimuth = {-25.8345 deg, 9.5445 deg, 22.1663 deg, 85.3141 deg}
equations.purpose: Renders the same four Figure 1 time-of-day / Sun-position skydome views with the step 029 model. Azimuths are measured from the red-cross centers in the directly extracted Bruneton-column Figure 1 tiles.

equations.name: distance to top atmosphere boundary
equations.purpose: Finds the integration length from the observer to the top atmosphere boundary.

equations.name: Beer-Lambert transmittance
equations.expression: T = exp(-(beta_R * L_R + beta_M * L_M + beta_O3 * L_O3))
equations.purpose: Computes transmittance from observer to sample and sample to Sun.

equations.name: paper comparison no-ozone policy
equations.purpose: Matches the Bruneton 2016 comparison implementation policy that neglects ozone absorption.

equations.name: single-scattering integrand
equations.expression: dL = T_view * T_sun * density(h) * beta(lambda) * solarIrradiance(lambda) * phase(nu) * ds
equations.purpose: Accumulates Rayleigh and Mie single-scattered radiance along the view ray.

equations.name: directional second-order scattering
equations.expression: dL_2 = T_view * density(h) * integral(L_1(omega_i) * beta(lambda) * phase(dot(view, omega_i)) d omega_i) * ds
equations.purpose: Replaces the scalar proxy with an explicit second-scattering integral over a finite set of incoming sky directions.

equations.name: Fibonacci full-sphere second-order quadrature
equations.expression: omega_i from a spherical Fibonacci lattice; integral_S2 f(omega) d omega ~= (4*pi/N) * sum_i f(omega_i)
equations.purpose: Replaces the earlier upper-hemisphere/two-ring second-order directions with a deterministic full-sphere quadrature, addressing the paper's diagnosis that an 8-direction single-plane approximation misses many incoming directions.

equations.name: paper sky-radiance direct-Sun omission
equations.expression: L_display(lambda) = L_sky_scattered(lambda); L_sun_direct(lambda) is not added to the camera pass
equations.purpose: Tests the Figure 1 target contract where the visible comparison target is sky radiance/aureole and the Sun direction is indicated by an overlay marker.

equations.name: Bruneton RGB radiance wavelengths
equations.expression: lambda_R = 680 nm, lambda_G = 550 nm, lambda_B = 440 nm
equations.purpose: Stores radiance in Bruneton's 3-wavelength RGB radiance API order.

equations.name: Bruneton luminance spectral samples
equations.purpose: Uses the same centered wavelength-bin strategy Bruneton applies in precomputed illuminance mode, here evaluated directly for each skydome pixel.

equations.name: direct solar radiance separated from sky pass
equations.purpose: Defines the direct solar beam term that this sky-radiance target-contract step keeps separate from displayed atmospheric sky radiance.

equations.name: Bruneton 2016 Figure 1 display transform
equations.purpose: Audits the Figure 1 paper display contract after CIE integration and XYZ-to-linear-sRGB conversion, using the comparison source implementation k = 1 / (5 * 683).

equations.name: Bruneton comparison source Figure 1 tone-map k
equations.purpose: Uses the same reciprocal display scale as Bruneton's clear-sky comparison source ToneMapping function.

equations.name: Bruneton radiance-to-luminance factors
equations.expression: k_c = 683 * integral((XYZ_TO_SRGB_c dot CIE(lambda)) * E_sun(lambda) / E_sun(lambda_c) * (lambda / lambda_c)^p d lambda)
equations.purpose: Approximates CIE/XYZ/sRGB luminance conversion from three spectral radiance samples.

secondOrderScattering.incidentRadianceCacheCoordinates: altitude bin for each incoming direction

display.colorRole: Fifteen spectral radiance samples integrated with CIE 1931 color matching functions and XYZ to linear sRGB before the paper Figure 1 tone map.
display.transform: 1 - exp(-k * max(0, linear_sRGB)); k is Bruneton comparison source k = 1 / (5 * 683)
display.outsideCircle: Transparent alpha marks pixels outside the sky dome.

omittedByDesign: direct solar-disc radiance in the camera pass; this step isolates atmospheric sky radiance and aureole for the Figure 1 target-contract test
third and higher scattering orders; a directional second-order term is included
full Bruneton precomputed illuminance textures; this evaluates 15 spectral samples directly per pixel
